Weather & Cloud Parameterization defines the physical and visual properties for volumetric cloud rendering, controlling coverage, density, type, geometry, lighting, and noise interaction [S1, S2, unofficial].

The claim states that 'Weather & Cloud Parameterization' defines physical and visual properties for volumetric cloud rendering, specifically controlling coverage, density, type, geometry, lighting, and noise interaction. Source [S1] explicitly notes that the 'Weather' struct defines 'physical and visual parameters for volumetric cloud rendering, controlling coverage, density, type, geometry, lighting, and noise interaction.' It further lists specific fields for coverage, density, cloudType (type), baseHeight/thickness (geometry), sunAzimuth/Elevation/Intensity/Anisotropy (lighting), and erosion (noise interaction). Source [S2] provides implementation details on how coverage affects density, supporting the functional description. Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
